          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:

          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized to E.164 form:
            spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and country code
            are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and is the value stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20

## Summary

I implemented `namesakeCount` on the owner-create flow so that a created owner reports how many existing owners already shared its first and last name (case-insensitively) at creation time.

Changes:

- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after assigning the customer code, computes `countNamesakes(firstName, lastName)` and stores it on the owner. The new `countNamesakes` helper counts existing owners whose first *and* last names match case-insensitively (via a `normalizeName` lowercasing helper), evaluated against `findAllOwners()` *before* the new owner is saved — so it excludes the owner being created.
- **`Owner` entity** (`model/Owner.java`) — added a nullable `Integer namesakeCount` field mapped to a new `namesake_count` column, with getter/setter following the existing `customerCode`/`householdId` pattern.
- **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` integer property to the `Owner` response schema (regenerates the `OwnerDto`, which MapStruct auto-maps by name).
- **Schema DDL** — added `namesake_count INTEGER` to the `owners` table in all four DB scripts (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres). The test profile uses hsqldb with `ddl-auto=none`, so the column had to be declared explicitly.

The new `Cp13Tests` passes (two owners sharing `firstName`+`lastName` → the second gets `namesakeCount = 1`), and the full 22-test suite is green.
